tip: The 는 (neun) tucked into 생각하지는 않아요 (saenggakajineun anayo) makes the denial partial: with 꼭 (kkok = necessarily), it reads 'I don't necessarily think so', not a flat no.
-다고 생각해요 = I think that: 좋다고 생각해요 (jotago saenggakaeyo) = I think it's good.
것 같아요 softens a claim into an impression: 맞는 것 같아요 (manneun geot gatayo) = it seems right.
일리가 있다 = to have a point: 일리가 있어요 (illiga isseoyo).
-지는 않지만 (-jineun anchiman) = 'not exactly X, but': 확실하지는 않지만 (hwaksilhajineun anchiman) = I'm not certain, but... The 는 makes the denial partial.
A verb plus 보다 (boda = see) means try it: 생각해 볼게요 (saenggakae bolgeyo) = I'll try thinking it over.
-야 하다 = have to: 고민해야 해요 (gominhaeya haeyo) = we have to think it over.
-에 따라 = depending on: 상황에 따라 (sanghwang-e ttara).
Koreans rarely say a flat no – 아닌 것 같아요 (anin geot gatayo) = 'it seems not so' turns disagreement into an impression, which is the polite default.
-는 건 아니에요 (-neun geon anieyo) = 'it's not that I...': 반대하는 건 아니에요 (bandaehaneun geon anieyo) denies only the framing, not the whole idea.
왜냐하면 (waenyahamyeon) opens the reason and normally closes with -기 때문이에요: 부족하기 때문이에요 (bujokagi ttaemunieyo). The reason is marked at both ends.
-에 따르면 = according to: 통계에 따르면 (tonggye-e ttareumyeon).
-을 근거로 = based on: 경험을 근거로 (gyeongheomeul geungeoro).
-면 안 되다 = must not: 말하면 안 돼요 (malhamyeon an dwaeyo).
-(으)ㄹ까 봐 = worried that: 줄일까 봐 (juril-kka bwa).
없이는 = without: 스마트폰 없이는 (seumateupon eopsineun).
위주 (wiju) after a noun = -centered: 시험 위주 (siheom wiju) = exam-focused.
살기 좋다 = good to live in: 살기 좋아요 (salgi joayo).
Influence is something you give in Korean: 영향을 줘요 (yeonghyangeul jwoyo) = literally 'gives influence'. Same with stress or help – 주다 (juda = give) does the work.
-지 마세요 (-ji maseyo) is the polite 'please don't': 믿지 마세요 (mitji maseyo) = please don't trust. It attaches to the bare verb stem, whatever the verb.
-는 편이다 = tend to: 찬성하는 편이에요 (chanseonghaneun pyeonieyo).
꼭 (kkok = necessarily) plus a negative = 'not necessarily': 꼭 그렇다고 볼 수는 없어요 (kkok geureotago bol suneun eopseoyo) = you can't necessarily see it that way.
보니 = now that I've done it and see: 생각해 보니 (saenggakae boni) = now that I think about it.
-고 보니 = after doing: 듣고 보니 (deutgo boni).
귀를 기울이다 (gwireul giurida) is literally 'tilt an ear' – leaning in to listen. 귀를 기울여야 해요 (gwireul giuryeoya haeyo) = we should lend an ear.
-려고 (-ryeogo) marks purpose – 'in order to': 이해하려고 (ihaeharyeogo) = in order to understand. The goal comes before the trying, the reverse of English order.
-겠습니다 states a formal announced future: 도착하겠습니다 (dochakagetseumnida = will arrive).
-음을 알려 드립니다 is the formal 'we hereby inform you that': 선정되셨음을 알려 드립니다 (seonjeongdoesyeosseumeul allyeo deurimnida).
-이/가 있겠습니다 announces an event formally: 입장이 있겠습니다 (ipjang-i itgetseumnida = there will be an entrance).
삼가 (samga = respectfully) opens formal condolences: 명복을 빌며 (myeongbogeul bilmyeo = praying for the repose of the deceased).
